title: Epic: Lint Rules
description: type: epic

title: Story: Horizontal alignment lint for adjacent boxes
description:
Detect misalignment between horizontally adjacent boxes — the most common multi-box layout.

Target pattern:
```
┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐   ┌─────────┐
│  Step 1  │──►│  Step 2  │──►│  Step 3  │
└─────────┘   └─────────┘   └─────────┘
```

Lint rules:
1. Adjacent boxes (connected by a horizontal arrow or within N columns of each other) should share the same top row
2. Adjacent boxes should share the same bottom row
3. Spacing between adjacent boxes should be consistent (if box A→B has 3 cols gap, B→C should too)
4. Vertically stacked boxes should share the same left column

Detection:
- Two boxes are 'adjacent' if connected by an arrow or if their vertical extents overlap and horizontal gap is < 10 columns
- Group adjacent boxes into rows and columns
- Check alignment within each group

Example from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Lines 51-57: Kyverno and ArgoCD boxes should share top/bottom rows
- Lines 81-85: S3 and DynamoDB boxes should share top rows
- Lines 90-94: two Lambda boxes should align

Acceptance criteria:
- Reports which boxes are misaligned and by how many rows/columns
- Suggests the correction direction (e.g., 'move box down 1 row')
- Does not flag boxes that are intentionally at different vertical positions (e.g., in a flowchart with multiple tiers)
- Grouping heuristic correctly identifies adjacent vs. unrelated boxes

title: Epic: Core Parser

title: Story: Embedded diagram extraction (pipe/stdin-first)
description:
Support diagrams embedded in larger documents — markdown code blocks, comment-prefixed lines, indented fragments.

This is critical for real-world usage. Most diagrams are not standalone files. They are:
- Indented by 4 spaces inside a markdown code block
- Prefixed with // or # on every line (in source code comments)
- A 3-box fragment, not a full-page architecture diagram
- Piped via stdin from another tool or editor

Approach:
1. Detect common prefix patterns (consistent leading whitespace, comment markers)
2. Strip the prefix, lint/fix the diagram, re-add the prefix
3. When reading from stdin, auto-detect whether input is a raw diagram or embedded

Supported prefix patterns:
- Uniform indentation (N spaces or tabs)
- Line comment markers: //, #, --, ;, *, %
- Combinations: '    // ' (indented comment)
- Markdown fenced code blocks (extract content between backtick fences)

Acceptance criteria:
- `echo "$diagram" | boxlint fix` works for raw diagrams
- `boxlint fix --strip-prefix='// '` handles comment-prefixed diagrams
- Auto-detection correctly identifies indentation-only vs comment-prefixed
- Prefix is restored exactly after fix (same whitespace, same comment marker)
- Partial diagrams (single box, single arrow) lint without errors about 'missing' structure
- Works with `boxlint lint -` and `boxlint fix -` for explicit stdin

title: Story: Implement box detection and parsing
description:
Detect rectangular boxes in the grid by finding matching corner characters and verifying edge integrity.

Approach:
- Scan for ┌ (top-left corner), trace right to find ┐, trace down to find ┘, verify └ closes the rectangle
- Validate all edge characters are correct (─ for horizontal, │ for vertical)
- Support nested boxes (box inside box)
- Extract box interior content as raw text

Lint-relevant output per box:
- BoundingRect { top_left: (row, col), bottom_right: (row, col) }
- Edge character positions (for corner/edge alignment checks)
- Interior text content (for content alignment checks)

Example from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Line 2-4: title box (full-width)
- Line 11-22: Developer Laptop box
- Line 49-73: large Actuation Layer box containing nested boxes

Edge cases:
- Boxes sharing edges (adjacent boxes)
- Nested boxes (GA Workflow inside GitHub box, lines 14-21)
- Single-row or single-column boxes (degenerate)

Acceptance criteria:
- Correctly finds all boxes in demo-flow-diagram.txt
- Returns bounding rects with accurate positions
- Handles nested boxes without double-counting
- Performance: < 10ms for a 200-line diagram

title: Story: Implement line and arrow detection
description:
Detect lines and arrows in the grid — horizontal (─, ═), vertical (│, ║), and their directional endpoints (►, ▼, ◄, ▲, >, <, v, ^).

Approach:
- Trace contiguous runs of line-drawing characters
- Classify each segment as horizontal or vertical
- Detect arrow tips at segment endpoints
- Handle multi-segment paths (L-shaped, T-shaped connectors)
- INLINE LABELS: detect and skip text embedded in arrow segments (e.g., ──POST──► or ──git push──►). The label is the text between line-drawing characters. Store label text and position but do not treat label characters as part of the line geometry.

Output per line/arrow:
- Segments: list of (start_pos, end_pos, direction)
- Arrow tips: position + direction
- Whether the line connects to a box edge
- Inline label: Option<(text, start_pos, end_pos)>

Example from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Line 12: ────────────► (horizontal arrow with right tip)
- Lines 25-28: vertical connector from GitHub box down to ConfigHub
- Line 105: multi-hop chain with inline labels: Browser ──POST──► Lambda ──► DynamoDB ──► EventBridge

Edge cases:
- Arrows with inline text labels (line 12: 'git push' label between segments)
- Dashed lines (line 99: ─ ─ ─ separator)
- Double-line borders (═══) vs single (───)
- Label text containing characters that look like line-drawing (rare but possible)

Acceptance criteria:
- Correctly identifies all arrows in demo-flow-diagram.txt
- Distinguishes arrows from box edges
- Inline labels are extracted with correct positions and text content
- Dashed separators classified separately from solid connectors
- Arrow geometry (start, end, direction) is correct even when labels are present

title: Story: Fix box corner and edge alignment
description:
Auto-fix boxes with misaligned corners or broken edges.

Fix strategies:
1. Replace incorrect corner characters with correct ones (e.g., + → ┌)
2. Fill gaps in horizontal edges with ─
3. Fill gaps in vertical edges with │
4. If a corner is missing entirely, insert it (may shift content)

Constraints:
- Fixes must not alter box interior content
- Fixes must not change box dimensions (no resizing)
- When ambiguous, prefer the fix that preserves surrounding layout

Acceptance criteria:
- For each diagnostic from box corner lint (boxlint-lll), produces a corrected output
- Round-trip: fix then lint produces zero diagnostics for the fixed issues
- Original content inside boxes is preserved byte-for-byte
- ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY: running boxlint fix on a diagram with no corner/edge issues MUST produce byte-identical output. The fixer is a no-op on clean input. Test this explicitly.

title: Story: Build diagram IR and grid model
description:
Parse raw UTF-8 text into a structured intermediate representation (IR). Build a character grid from the input, then identify structural regions (boxes, lines, text) as IR nodes with positions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Input: raw string of a box-drawing diagram
- Output: Grid struct (2D char array with row/col indexing) + DiagramIR struct containing typed nodes
- Grid correctly handles Unicode box-drawing characters (single-width: ─│┌┐└┘├┤┬┴┼, double: ═║ etc.)
- Handles mixed-width content (ASCII + box-drawing chars)
- Preserves original line:col positions for diagnostics
- Handles empty input, single-line input, and ragged lines (unequal lengths)

Reference: demo-flow-diagram.txt (135 lines, nested boxes, arrows, labels)

title: Epic: Auto-Fixer
description: type: epic

title: Story: Fix horizontal alignment for adjacent boxes
description:
Auto-fix horizontally misaligned adjacent boxes by shifting box positions.

Fix strategies:
1. Align top rows of adjacent boxes to the topmost box in the group
2. Extend shorter boxes downward to match the tallest (add edge rows)
3. Normalize spacing between adjacent boxes to the most common gap
4. When shifting a box, move its interior content and connected arrows

Constraints:
- Never overlap boxes
- Preserve arrow connections (re-route if box moves)
- If fixing would require moving a box more than 3 rows, report as unfixable

Acceptance criteria:
- Adjacent boxes share top and bottom rows after fix
- Spacing between boxes is consistent after fix
- Arrow connections preserved after box movement
- ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY: running boxlint fix on already-aligned adjacent boxes MUST produce byte-identical output. The fixer is a no-op on clean input. Test this explicitly.

title: Story: Set up CI pipeline
description:
Set up GitHub Actions CI for the Rust project. Adapted from stringer's Go CI pipeline.

Jobs:
- test: cargo build + cargo test on stable and MSRV (1.75)
- clippy: cargo clippy with -D warnings
- fmt: cargo fmt --check
- commit-lint: conventional commits validation on PRs
- backlog-health: beads orphan check on PRs

Acceptance criteria:
- Workflow runs on push to main and PRs to main
- Fails on clippy warnings or formatting issues
- Tests run on both stable and MSRV
- Conventional commit messages enforced on PRs

title: Story: Fix box sizing for content
description:
Auto-fix boxes whose dimensions don't fit their content.

Fix strategies:
1. Widen boxes where text overflows right edge (extend ─ and move ┐/┘)
2. Re-center title text after widening
3. Pad content lines to consistent width within the box

Constraints:
- Only resize the minimum amount needed
- Widening a box must not overlap with adjacent boxes (warn if it would)
- Preserve relative alignment of connected arrows where possible

Acceptance criteria:
- Overflow text is fully contained after fix
- Box edges are straight and corners correct after resize
- Connected arrows are flagged if they need adjustment (don't silently break them)
- ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY: running boxlint fix on a diagram where all content fits its boxes MUST produce byte-identical output. The fixer is a no-op on clean input. Test this explicitly.

title: Story: Arrow and connector lint
description:
Detect misaligned arrows, connectors, and their connections to boxes. Covers both arrow-to-box attachment points and connector segment alignment (horizontal/vertical straightness).

Subsumes former 'Connector alignment lint' story (boxlint-yyg).

Lint rules:
1. Arrow endpoints must touch a box edge (not float in space)
2. Arrow endpoints must connect at a box edge midpoint or corner, not arbitrary positions
3. Horizontal arrow segments (─, ─►) must share the same row
4. Vertical arrow segments (│, ▼) must share the same column
5. Arrow direction indicators (►, ▼, ◄, ▲) must face the target box

Example violations from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Line 12: arrow ────────────► lands on │ of GitHub box (off-by-one from box edge?)
- Line 68: long composition label causes box edge alignment issues

Acceptance criteria:
- All 5 rules produce diagnostics with line:col positions
- Each diagnostic includes a human-readable explanation
- False positive rate < 5% on demo-flow-diagram.txt

title: Story: Box corner and edge alignment lint
description:
Detect boxes with misaligned corners or irregular edges.

Lint rules:
1. All four corners of a box must use correct characters (┌ top-left, ┐ top-right, └ bottom-left, ┘ bottom-right)
2. Top and bottom edges must be continuous ─ characters (no gaps)
3. Left and right edges must be continuous │ characters (no gaps)
4. Corners must form a proper rectangle (top-left and top-right on same row, top-left and bottom-left on same column)
5. Mixed corner styles (e.g., ┌ with ╗) should warn

Example violations from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Verify all ~20 boxes have matching corners and straight edges
- Watch for off-by-one in wide boxes like lines 78-96

Acceptance criteria:
- Reports line:col of each misaligned corner or broken edge
- Diagnostic message names the expected vs actual character
- Zero false positives on well-formed boxes in demo-flow-diagram.txt
- Catches intentionally broken boxes in test fixtures

title: Story: Box content alignment lint
description:
Detect text content inside boxes that is misaligned or overflows box boundaries.

Lint rules:
1. Text must not extend beyond the left or right box edges
2. Text should be consistently aligned within a box (all left-aligned, all centered, or all right-aligned — warn on mixed)
3. Single-line centered titles (like line 3) should be centered within 1 char tolerance
4. Content lines should not be empty padding beyond 1 row top/bottom

Example from demo-flow-diagram.txt:
- Line 3: title text should be centered in the full-width box
- Lines 15-21: multi-line content in Developer Laptop box should be left-aligned
- Lines 32-40: ConfigHub content alignment

Acceptance criteria:
- Reports line:col of misaligned text with expected alignment
- Distinguishes intentional whitespace from alignment errors
- Handles boxes with mixed content (labels + values) like the ConfigHub box

title: Story: Scaffold Rust project
description:
Initialize the Rust project with Cargo.toml, src/main.rs entry point, and basic module structure (parser, linter, fixer modules as empty stubs). Include clap dependency for future CLI work.

Acceptance criteria:
- cargo build succeeds
- cargo test runs (even with no tests yet)
- Module stubs exist: src/parser.rs, src/linter.rs, src/fixer.rs
- Reasonable Cargo.toml with project metadata

title: Story: Implement CLI with lint and fix subcommands
description:
Implement the boxlint CLI with lint and fix subcommands using clap.

Usage:
  boxlint lint <file>         # Print diagnostics to stderr, exit 1 if any
  boxlint lint --format json  # JSON output for editor integration  
  boxlint fix <file>          # Auto-fix and write to stdout
  boxlint fix <file> -i       # Auto-fix in place
  boxlint lint <dir>          # Lint all .txt files in directory

Acceptance criteria:
- clap-based arg parsing with help text
- lint subcommand loads file, runs all registered lint rules, prints diagnostics
- Diagnostic format: file:line:col: level: message (gcc-style)
- JSON output mode for IDE integration (LSP-compatible format)
- fix subcommand runs fixers and outputs corrected text
- Exit code 0 = clean, 1 = lint errors found, 2 = usage error
- --quiet flag suppresses warnings, shows only errors
- Reads from stdin if no file argument given

title: Story: Fix arrow-to-box connections
description:
Auto-fix arrows that don't properly connect to box edges.

Fix strategies:
1. Extend or shorten arrow segments so endpoints land on a box edge
2. Adjust arrow tip position to touch the nearest box edge
3. Re-align arrow segments that are off by 1 row/column

Constraints:
- Don't change which boxes the arrow connects
- Don't change arrow direction
- If the fix would require moving more than 2 characters, report as unfixable

Acceptance criteria:
- For each diagnostic from arrow lint (boxlint-goq), produces a corrected output
- Round-trip: fix then lint produces zero arrow-connection diagnostics
- Arrows still point in the correct direction after fixing
- ROUND-TRIP FIDELITY: running boxlint fix on a diagram where all arrows connect correctly MUST produce byte-identical output. The fixer is a no-op on clean input. Test this explicitly.
